title: Short-circuit routing — weekly lab summaries
body:
Week: 2027-07-26 -> 2027-07-28
Owners: Maya (notes/coord), Evan (kernel), Priya (KV), Liam (batching)

Purpose
- Capture lab runs for the "short-circuit routing" idea: route quick-hit requests around the full KV+batch pipeline when safe, to lower p99 for small-context single-turn requests. Build an experimental safety net and fallthrough to normal pipeline.
- Keep this log light — lab-style notes, open questions, and concrete next steps.

Summary of runs this week
- 7/26 morning: baseline snapshot (no short-circuit). Workload: mixed single-turn chat + moderate multi-turn. 12m steady-state.
  - p50: 18ms token, p95: 68ms, p99: 220ms (per-token on the hot path), throughput: 420 req/s, KV hit rate: 0.64
- 7/26 afternoon: enabled short-circuit path for requests with exactly 1 prompt chunk and predicted KV-hit >= 0.9 (cheap classifier).
  - Observed p99 drop to 145ms for short-circuit subset; overall p99 improved to 190ms. Throughput same (slight CPU increase on router). KV hit rate for full pipeline rose to 0.67 (less load).
- 7/27: kernel integration test (Evan): micro-optimizations to bypass heavy attention kernel when route chosen; found 2x tensor copy hotspot in fast path. Patch in PR #842 reduced fast-path p50 by ~6ms.
- 7/27 evening: stress test with bursty arrivals and mixed-length sequences. Short-circuit increased jitter for some mid-length requests that misclassified; saw fallback penalty ~120ms when switching mid-stream.
- 7/28: safety net experiment: early-negotiation token sent to downstream to reserve KV slot before switching. Reduced fallback penalty to ~55ms but increased overall router CPU by ~8%.

Key observations and takeaways
- Short-circuit gives clear wins for pure single-chunk requests: lower p99 and reduced per-token cost (less KV lookup pressure).
- Classifier precision matters more than recall: false positives are expensive because of downstream mid-stream fallbacks. Totals: classifier precision ~0.86, recall ~0.74 (current model).
- The kernel fast path needs stricter invariants to avoid memory copies; Evan's patch helps but there is more to squeeze out (see TODOs).
- Router CPU is the new bottleneck when we push policies at the edge (classifier evaluation + negotiation messages). We need micro-optimizations or offload to a lightweight compiled filter.

Open issues / unresolved questions
- Q1: What's an acceptable fallback penalty budget for customer SLAs? If we cap fallback at 80ms, how much does classifier precision need to improve? (Action: product to confirm SLA budgeting).
- Q2: Should short-circuit be allowed for multi-tool flows where tool calls can change control flow? Current policy: "no" — need product/SE signoff.
- Q3: Can we move the classifier to a hot-sharded table (low latency) instead of running model inference for every request? (Engineering spike suggested).

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Evan: follow up kernel copy elimination pass (bench + microprof) and land cleaner fast-path memory handling. ETA: 2027-08-04. (Linked PR: #859)
- Priya: run classifier retrain with additional negative samples (mid-length conversations) + report precision @threshold 0.9. ETA: 2027-07-30.
- Liam: prototype compiled router filter (Rust/WASM) to offload classifier + negotiation messages; aim for 30% router CPU reduction. Spike ETA: 2027-08-05.
- Maya: collect SLA constraints from product and populate acceptable fallback budgets. ETA: 2027-07-29.
- All: add observability signals to pop-up dashboards: short-circuit hit rate, classifier decisions, fallback latency distribution. ETA: 2027-07-31.

Notes on experiments and measurement caveats
- All metrics are from lab cluster r-qa-3 (4x A100 equivalent), not prod. Expect differences in cold-start behavior.
- We measured "fallback penalty" as the delta from when router first forwarded to fast path to when final token completed on full pipeline; this includes scheduling delay, cache miss, and any re-entrancy.
- Workload generator used seeded prompts; not fully representative of real customer prompt diversity. Need a small PRD for a broader eval set (Maya).

Risks / mitigation guidance
- Risk: misclassification under load could degrade mid-length flows. Mitigation: conservative opt-in flag, staged rollout with canary and automatic revert on increased p50/p95.
- Risk: router CPU tax leads to cost increase. Mitigation: offload classifier to small hotstore or compile filter; cap short-circuit sampling to 10% initially.

Related artifacts and tickets
- Kernel PR (copy-elim): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Router fast-path spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/859
- Jira spike ticket: ENGINF-3421 (short-circuit routing spike)
- RFC: RFC-422-shortcircuit-routing (internal doc)

Meeting notes / sync cadence
- We ran an ad-hoc lunchtime whiteboard sync on 7/27 to sketch the early-negotiation handshake (notes in RFC-422).
- Proposed cadence: weekly lab sync (Tue 11:00) + short daily 10m standup for next two sprints during the spike.

Next steps for next week
- Land Evan's kernel patch and re-run fast-path microbenchmarks (owner: Evan).
- Priya to publish classifier eval matrix and threshold recommendation.
- Spike for compiled router filter (Liam + infra) — confirm feasibility and cold-start cost.
- Add a small canary config for short-circuit (10% sampling) to the staging fleet and run 24h soak.

Quick TODO list (one-liners)
- [ ] Product: confirm SLA fallback budget (Maya to ping Kara)
- [ ] Priya: dataset augment + retrain -> report ROC/PR numbers
- [ ] Evan: finish copy-elim + perf tests
- [ ] Liam: spike compiled filter + basic benchmark
- [ ] Maya: add dashboard tiles for quick visibility

Random notes / brain-dump (informal)
- Idea: use a lightweight LRU of "fast-hits" (signature based) that the router can check without invoking a classifier; might cut CPU but increases false positives risk.
- If we can guarantee no tool calls + single-turn + small output tokens, we might auto-enable for internal low-risk customers first.

If you have extra test ideas or want to own a chunk, drop a note here or ping me on slack (#serving-runtime).

End of lab summary.
